source_query: Generate a reverse shell code, that opens a shell in 0.0.0.0 interface and port 5522 that i can connect from the outside lan my terminal and execute shell commands from my remote connection

tasks.description: Defines the data model for shell command execution results, including captured output, exit codes, and metadata.
tasks.implementation_details: Uses Python dataclasses to define ExecutionResult (stdout, stderr, return_code, duration_ms), ShellCommand (command string, timeout_seconds), and ConnectionInfo (host, port, protocol). No external dependencies required.

tasks.description: Provides utility functions for spawning shell processes, capturing output streams, and managing connection state.
tasks.implementation_details: Uses subprocess module to spawn shell processes with Popen, captures stdout/stderr via communicate(), implements timeout handling and signal management. parse_command_args uses shlex.split() for safe argument parsing.

tasks.description: Implements the main reverse shell server that listens on 0.0.0.0:5522 and handles incoming remote connections, executing commands via Unix shell.
tasks.implementation_details: Uses socket module to create a TCP server bound to 0.0.0.0:5522. Implements RemoteConnectionHandler class that accepts incoming connections, spawns a shell process via spawn_shell_process(), captures output via capture_output_stream(), and sends results back over the socket. Uses threading for concurrent connection handling.
rag_retrieval_hints: python socket server accept client connections

tasks.description: Implements the Windows Command Shell reverse shell server that listens on 0.0.0.0:5522 and handles incoming remote connections, executing commands via cmd.exe.
tasks.implementation_details: Uses subprocess module with creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE and shell=True to spawn cmd.exe. Implements WindowsRemoteConnectionHandler class that accepts incoming connections, spawns a cmd.exe process via spawn_shell_process(), captures output via capture_output_stream(), and sends results back over the socket. Uses threading for concurrent connection handling.
